title: Cardini 2018 maternal brain gain preprint trunk PPS
citation: Cardini, F., Fatemi-Ghomi, N., Gajewska-Knapik, K., Gooch, V., & Aspell, J. E. (2018). Maternal brain gain: enlarged representation of peripersonal space in pregnancy. bioRxiv 492017.
notes: Run one 65-trial trunk PPS assessment for a selected visit. The synthesized headphone cue preserves the 3-second pink noise duration and relative level rise. The original study requires two calibrated speakers, the abdominal tapper and left-hand response hardware.

reported_source.type: Two copies of the same pink noise with opposing level envelopes.
reported_source.near_speaker_reference: Close to the left response hand.

reported_tactile_response.response: Press with the left hand promptly after touch and ignore sound.

reference_parameters.reported_analysis: Use session-specific delay-by-group ANOVAs and compare participant linear slopes within each session after excluding fits below R² .20.
reference_parameters.profile_scope: One 65-trial assessment per visit. Repeat with the reported longitudinal visit schedule.
remaining_caveats: The generated headphone cue uses the 15 dB reported level change as a digital envelope. Original near and far speaker envelopes and body-relative source coordinates remain unavailable. Toolkit path and azimuth are illustration settings.

For the study procedure use a calibrated mechanical abdominal tapper with a synchronized left-hand button and the published blindfolded setup. Preview output is a tactile-channel marker and a mouse response. Tap drive, pulse length, force and physical latencies require verification.
The original trial order, foreperiod, end silence, intertrial timing and response deadline remain unspecified. The toolkit uses a seeded shuffle and its normal response and trial timing defaults.

provenance.field: Longitudinal visits, sounds, touch, response and trial allocation
provenance.source: https://doi.org/10.1101/492017, pp. 8–10, Participants, Procedure and Fig. 2
